observation_summary: When deserializing nested reference types (e.g., AtomicReference<AtomicReference<Integer>>), deserializing a null value results in an incorrect object structure (an AtomicReference containing null instead of an AtomicReference containing an AtomicReference containing null).
hypothesis: The root cause is twofold: (1) The AtomicReferenceDeserializer's getNullValue method incorrectly initializes a new empty AtomicReference instead of using the contextual null value provider. (2) Various SettableBeanProperty implementations fail to keep the value deserializer and the null value provider in sync when creating new contextual instances.
prediction: The fix will involve updating AtomicReferenceDeserializer to use the value deserializer's null value, and updating the copy constructors of various property classes to ensure the null value provider is correctly synchronized with the updated deserializer.
experiment_rationale: The provided diff shows exactly these changes: AtomicReferenceDeserializer now calls _valueDeserializer.getNullValue(ctxt), and the property classes now calculate the null value provider (nvp) by checking if the deserializer and provider were originally linked, ensuring they remain in sync.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves correcting the initialization logic for null values in the deserializer and ensuring that the null value provider is correctly assigned/synchronized during property object creation. This is a classic Assignment/Initialization defect where the state (the null provider) is not correctly initialized or propagated.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows changes to AtomicReferenceDeserializer.getNullValue to use _valueDeserializer.getNullValue(ctxt) instead of new AtomicReference().

The fix_diff_oracle shows changes to multiple property classes (CreatorProperty, FieldProperty, etc.) to calculate the correct NullValueProvider (nvp) during object creation to keep it in sync with the deserializer.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic was updated, the core issue is the incorrect initialization of the null value and the failure to maintain the correct state (the null provider) during object creation, which fits Assignment/Initialization better.
